rationale:
Evidence: the iteration-0 design (base_speed 1.7, kp 2.0, kd 0.1, ki 0.02, sensors at y 0.05, footprint 0.012, mass 0.8) went off track in all 60 trials. Progress was only 0.035 to 0.115, max_error reached the 0.06 m limit, and each run had one line-loss event. The robot left the line early, not gradually. I accept the critique's main point: the failure happens too early for a slow drift, and the draft changed too many things at once to learn from. I also accept that base_speed 1.2 cuts the speed the time term needs, so I do not go that low.

What I changed, and why:
(1) base_speed 1.7 to 1.3. The race data show the robot cannot hold the line at 1.7 with this steering. Staying on the line is the precondition for any score, so I lower speed to a level between the failed 1.7 and the untested 1.2. This is a judgement, since no PWM-to-ground-speed mapping is given.
(2) kp 2.0 to 3.0. Stronger steering correction is needed to hold the line at speed. kp 3 gives up to 1050 PWM of differential at full signal, which is within range.
(3) kd 0.1 to 0.15. Damping is raised moderately. I reject the critique's kd 0.3 for now. At 0.3, a signal change of 0.02 per 10 ms step already gives a turn term of about 0.6, and sharper changes saturate the wheels. kd 0.15 is a bounded step up.
(4) ki kept at 0.02 to offset the seeded left/right motor mismatch. Its maximum contribution is about 14 PWM, so windup is small.

Kept unchanged, so the race isolates speed and steering gains: sensor size 0.012, sensor spacing and y = 0.05, sensor weights, mass 0.8, wheel geometry, body, and line_loss last_direction. I keep body_width 0.12. The off-track limit is 0.06 m across the allowed range, so the value is neutral.

Decision rule for the next revision: if the robot still leaves the line before progress 0.5 (line_loss_events of 1 or more, max_error at 0.06), lower base_speed to 1.1 before changing gains. If it stays on track but does not finish, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1. If steering_oscillation is high with max_error low, raise kd before lowering kp. Success means completion 1 with rms_error under 0.03 m.

Predictions are guesses, not expectations: progress should rise well above 0.115, and max_error should fall below 0.05 m on the oval and s-bend. The draft aims to reach the end of the course, not to finish in 3 s, so the time term is likely small until base_speed is raised.
